paper_records.paper_title: Superelastic shape memory alloy cables: Part I – Isothermal tension experiments
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2013-Superelastic shape memory alloy cables Part I – Isothermal tension experiments.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: 2013-Superelastic shape memory alloy cables Part I – Isothermal tension experiments.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Core prior art on multiwire superelastic NiTi cables under tension testing inter-wire friction and transformation.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Directly threatens T1 by proving inter-wire contact, friction, and hysteretic energy dissipation in NiTi wire bundles.
paper_records.method: Experimental testing with non-contact optical diagnostics and thermal imaging
paper_records.material_or_system: 7x7 right regular lay and 1x27 alternating lay superelastic NiTi cables
paper_records.loading_mode: Quasi-static isothermal uniaxial elongation under rigid end rotation constraint
paper_records.control_variables: Displacement rate (1e-5 to 4e-4 s^-1), room temperature (22 deg C), lubrication state
paper_records.independent_variables: Cable geometry (7x7 regular lay vs 1x27 alternating lay), dry vs synthetic oil lubrication, strain amplitude up to 12.5%
paper_records.dependent_variables: Axial force-strain response, reaction torque Mz, localized temperature rise Delta T, strain field via stereo DIC
paper_records.model_used: Idealized polar moment of inertia J0; exponential shakedown curve fits
paper_records.constitutive_model: Phenomenological shakedown laws (modeling deferred to Part II)
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Qualitative Coulomb friction assessment via dry vs lubricated testing
paper_records.experiment_used: Instron 5585 load frame, stereo DIC, Inframetrics SC1000 infrared radiometer, Futek reaction torque cell
paper_records.experimental_setup: Straight cable specimens clamped rigidly in pneumatic grips with hardened steel serrated jaws
paper_records.key_results: Lubrication had negligible impact on axial stress-strain response, proving static friction locks inter-wire slip during initial loading; 7x7 cables exhibited flat transformation plateaus (493 MPa load, 262 MPa unload) with propagating fronts, while 1x27 exhibited continuous work hardening; substantial reaction torque generated.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that multiwire NiTi cables exhibit inter-wire contact normal forces, high static friction, and severe cyclic shakedown.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not evaluate bending flexure or external transverse fluid confinement pressure; does not validate a predictive contact constitutive law.
directly_verified_statements: Lubrication does not noticeably alter the axial load-strain curves of 7x7 or 1x27 NiTi cables (Section 4.1, p. 3012).
7x7 cable exhibits localized transformation front propagation with localized rotation kinks (Section 4.2, p. 3014).
Contact indentations observed in SEM are pre-existing manufacturing artifacts from stranding and shape setting (Section 4.5, p. 3019).
inferred_statements: High inter-wire normal force in helical cables suppresses inter-wire slip until high axial strains are reached.
paper_records.limitations: Uniaxial tension only; constrained rotation boundary condition; isothermal slow strain rates.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Closes C5/T1 at existence level by demonstrating mutual contact in NiTi wire bundles; refutes overclaims that contact indentations were operational fretting wear.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 5 (load-strain curves), Fig. 8 (SEM micrographs of inter-wire contact indentations)

paper_records.paper_title: Superelastic Shape Memory Alloy Cables: Part II – Subcomponent Isothermal Responses
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2013-Superelastic shape memory alloy cables Part II – Subcomponent isothermal responses.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: 2013-Superelastic shape memory alloy cables Part II – Subcomponent isothermal responses.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Evaluates subcomponent wire mechanics and tests Costello analytical contact-kinematics modeling on NiTi cables.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Evaluates whether existing cable kinematics and contact formulations can predict multiwire NiTi response (T1, T3, H0b).
paper_records.method: Hierarchical experimental testing and analytical kinematic modeling
paper_records.material_or_system: Single NiTi wires, 1x7 strands, 1x19 cables, and 1x27 cables
paper_records.control_variables: Displacement rate, room temperature (22 deg C)
paper_records.independent_variables: Subcomponent level (individual wires, straight core, outer helical wires, complete strands)
paper_records.dependent_variables: Axial force-strain response, torque generation, comparison against Costello model
paper_records.model_used: Costello kinematic wire rope theory with linear elastic wire assumptions
paper_records.constitutive_model: Costello wire rope kinematics combined with single-wire experimental curves
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Line contact formulation with inter-wire radial pressure
paper_records.experiment_used: MTS / Instron load frames with custom wire untwisting grips
paper_records.experimental_setup: Individual wires dissected from cables and tested in tension to isolate base material response
paper_records.key_results: Costello cable theory matched 1x7 strands and shallow helix angles well, but severely deviated for 1x27 cables with steep helix angles (>20 deg); deviation was caused by neglecting local bending and twisting moments in outer wires, not by novel constitutive contact physics.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that shallow helix angle NiTi bundles behave closely to single wires; proves that model divergence at steep angles is due to kinematic reduction omissions.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove a failure of continuum contact mechanics; does not support the requirement of a new micro-coupling law H1.
directly_verified_statements: The Costello model divergence in 1x27 cables stems from the neglect of individual wire bending and twisting moments (Section 5.3, pp. 3035-3037).
Single wire responses closely match 1x7 strand response when normalized by metallic cross-sectional area (Section 4.2, p. 3028).
inferred_statements: For parallel or nearly-parallel wire bundles (like MP1), kinematic helix angle errors do not arise.
paper_records.limitations: Tension only; analytical model did not resolve full 3D frictional stick-slip.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Mandates conservative remediation of Reedlunn 2013 (Astra G07): model failure in steep helical cables cannot be cited as evidence that parallel NiTi bundles require new mechanics.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 11 (Costello model vs experiment for 1x7 and 1x27 cables)
